terms.meaning: A server address the app's pages call to ask for data or perform an action.
A record that says who is logged in, carried in a cookie the browser sends with each request.
A short code a person must enter to create an account.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and server setup
sections.what: Brings in the request and response tools, the session and storage helpers, and tells the framework to run this route on the standard Node.js server.
sections.why: The route needs to read sessions and save codes, so these helpers are required.

sections.name: generateCode
sections.title: Random invite code maker
sections.what: Builds an 8-character code from letters and digits, leaving out easily confused characters such as 0, O, 1 and I.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps codes easy to read and type.
sections.watch_out: Uses Math.random, which is not designed for secret values, so generated codes may be more guessable than expected.

sections.name: GET
sections.title: List all invite codes
sections.what: Returns every invite code to an admin, and refuses everyone else.
sections.why: Lets the admin see which codes exist and which have been used.
sections.watch_out: Anyone whose session has isAdmin set sees every code.

sections.name: POST
sections.title: Create an invite code
sections.what: Creates one invite code, using the admin's custom code if provided, or a random one otherwise.
sections.why: Lets the admin add codes whenever needed.
sections.watch_out: A custom code that already exists may be overwritten, since the check for existing codes is not visible here.

summary: Lets the admin list existing invite codes and create new ones, which people need in order to sign up.
purpose: Admin tool for managing the invite codes that control who can create an account.
why: Likely reason: sign-up is limited to invited people, so the admin needs a way to create codes.
how: First the route checks that the caller is an admin. A list request returns all codes. A create request reads an optional custom code, makes it uppercase, or generates a random 8-character code if none is given, then saves it.
inputs: A login session cookie. For creating a code, an optional code in the request body.
outputs: A JSON list of codes, or the code that was created. Non-admins get a Forbidden error with status 403.
risks: Custom codes are not checked for length or allowed characters. The code shows no check for duplicates, so an existing code may be replaced, depending on how createInviteCode works (that function is not in the packet).
debug: If codes do not appear, check the storage functions in lib/kv. If every call returns Forbidden, check the session logic in lib/session and whether isAdmin is set on the account.
